clue.text: Sam's abroad, going round representing his country

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun: the one who represents his country

indicators.note: going round suggests the letters are turned about and set in a fresh order

parts.note: the possessive's S counts here as a letter of the ten-letter pool

explanation.surface: Sam, travelling overseas, tours about as his nation's envoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' rearranges SAMSABROAD; the possessive S is used as a letter here, and 'abroad' is fodder, not a pointer to a foreign setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat of top rank is sent abroad to speak for his government.

clue.text: Sound man for the post

indicators.note: Sound at the head of the clue tells us a word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: A request for a man who handles the post sounds like a job advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' could be an adjective (a sound man, a reliable one); it is the signal that MALE is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters and parcels delivered by the postal service are collectively called the post.

clue.text: Poisoner catches general unawares

indicators.note: catches means one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, a poisoner
Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A poisoner ambushes an army commander who is caught off guard.
explanation.walkthrough: LEE inside ASP gives the answer; Lee as a general is a crossword stock name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is not conscious of what is going on, hence off guard.

clue.text: Firemen who don't put fires out

definitions.text: Firemen who don't put fires out

parts.words: Firemen who don't put fires out
parts.note: firemen here are the men who tend a boiler's fire, feeding it fuel rather than extinguishing it

explanation.surface: A joke about firefighters who fail at their job.
explanation.definitionFit: On steam ships and locomotives the men who shovelled coal into the furnaces were called firemen.

clue.text: At short notice, sent up information

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: Information dispatched hurriedly at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns the whole of AT + AD round, so ATAD reads upward as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures collected for reference or analysis count as information.

clue.text: Fresh red rose at the back of the altar

indicators.note: fresh means new, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly cut red rose has been placed behind the altar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' suggests a newly picked flower; it signals rearranging REDROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorated screen or wall rising behind a church altar is called this.

clue.text: One seen in a hanging basket?

definitions.text: One seen in a hanging basket?

parts.words: One seen in a hanging basket?
parts.note: the basket is not a garden planter but the gondola slung beneath a hot-air craft, holding its pilot

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders who might turn up in a hanging basket of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who flies hot-air craft stands in the wicker basket suspended beneath the envelope.

clue.text: Settles, but I need terms re-negotiated

indicators.note: re-negotiated terms are reworked, so these letters are set out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A negotiator agrees to settle on condition that the terms are revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-negotiated' rearranges INEEDTERMS; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a question is to decide or fix it conclusively.

clue.text: Novice leads expert in tie

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A beginner goes ahead of a skilled player in a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' puts L before ACE; 'tie' looks like a drawn game but means fasten, as with shoelaces.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten shoes is to do them up with a cord threaded through the eyelets.

clue.text: He sticks up for his employer

definitions.text: He sticks up for his employer

parts.words: He sticks up for his employer
parts.note: sticks up reads as defends, but means pastes notices on walls for whoever hired him

explanation.surface: A loyal worker who defends his boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A man paid to paste advertising placards onto walls and hoardings.

clue.text: Develop part of a revolver

indicators.note: part of means the letters run inside the words a revolver

explanation.surface: A gunsmith works on one component of a handgun.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'a revolver' (a-REVOLVEr).
explanation.definitionFit: To grow gradually into something more complex is to develop.

clue.text: Get ready and shave beforehand?

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
to pare is to shave or trim thinly

explanation.surface: A barber getting set up wonders whether to shave a customer first.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is in reverse order to the clue: 'beforehand' gives the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something ready in advance is to get it ready.

clue.text: City copy published in France

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun: a magazine that is published there

parts.note: Paris is the French capital city
to match is to copy or equal

explanation.surface: A city's copy of a document is printed in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris Match is a French weekly news magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a long-running French weekly magazine of news and photographs.

clue.text: Extensive property

parts.note: property is not land or an estate but a physical quality, the ability to be stretched

explanation.surface: A large estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchiness, the capacity to extend and spring back, is a physical quality of materials.

clue.text: Character of those who are different

indicators.note: different means the letters are made different by being rearranged

explanation.surface: The nature of people who stand apart from others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who are' is a link; 'different' rearranges THOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The distinctive spirit or guiding beliefs of a group are its character.

clue.text: Jailbird before the bench has to toe the line

parts.note: a con, short for convict, is a jailbird
a form is a long bench without a back, as in an old schoolroom

explanation.surface: A prisoner up before the magistrates has to behave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bench' suggests magistrates in court; here it is a FORM, a backless bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To obey rules and do what is expected is to toe the line.

clue.text: Restrict king in temporary quarters

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a camp provides temporary lodging
R, for Rex, is king

explanation.surface: A monarch is confined in makeshift lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: R (Latin rex) goes inside CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper or confine someone's freedom of action is to restrict it.

clue.text: Navigational aids for sailor on ship

indicators.note: on here means the sailor is aboard, within the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Guidance a sailor uses at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: TAR goes inside SS, the steamship abbreviation; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors once steered by celestial bodies, taking bearings from them at night.

clue.text: Buck up at the back!

definitions.meaning: of a horse, to rise up on the hind legs

explanation.surface: A sergeant shouts encouragement at stragglers.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse bucking rises on its hind legs; the hindmost position is behind everything else.

clue.text: Furnace where link is forged

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A furnace where a chain link is made by a smith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' rearranges LINK; 'where' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven for firing pottery or bricks is a furnace.

clue.text: Figures they may have to be filled

definitions.text: they may have to be filled
definitions.meaning: printed documents with blanks that one must complete

explanation.surface: Numbers on paperwork that someone needs to complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures are shapes or outlines; official papers with blanks must be completed in.

clue.text: Beer, if out East, won't cost you anything!

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the noun: a thing that is free

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is east on a compass

explanation.surface: Beer drunk out in the East is on the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BEERIF, then E for East follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift handed out for nothing is free of charge.

clue.text: It gives ships loading room to spare, maybe

indicators.note: maybe hints that the letters could form something else when reordered

explanation.surface: A harbour offers vessels more than enough space to take on cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'room to spare' reads as one phrase, but 'room' belongs to the definition and 'maybe' rearranges TOSPARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour town where vessels dock to take on and unload cargo.

clue.text: Models that should not be dropped

definitions.meaning: people who pose for an artist
easy catches in cricket, which a fielder ought to hold

explanation.surface: An instruction to treat fashion models with care.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a sitter is a very easy catch.
explanation.definitionFit: People posing for a painter are models; in cricket an easy catch must not be dropped.

clue.text: Steep as fluctuations in Spanish currency

definitions.note: a singular phrase standing for the plural units of money

indicators.note: fluctuations mean changes, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Steep swings in the value of Spain's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluctuations' rearranges STEEPAS; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain's money before the euro was counted in these coins.

clue.text: Charm, finish and musical ability

parts.note: an end is a finish
a good ear is a gift for music

explanation.surface: Three qualities in a performer: allure, polish and talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finish' suggests polish, but it gives END.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm is to make oneself loved or liked, as a verb.

clue.text: Agree one is about a month in arrears

indicators.note: is about means the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: in arrears means behind, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Dec is short for December

explanation.surface: A tenant consents, admitting rent is a month overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in arrears' turns DEC to CED, which goes inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede to a request is to consent or go along with it.

clue.text: A real eyesore

parts.note: eyesore reads as an ugly sight, but here is a literal sore on the eyelid

explanation.surface: Something truly ugly to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid is literally a painful spot by the eye.

clue.text: It's only fair

definitions.meaning: merely, as in only a little

explanation.surface: Something that is simply the right thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means merely, and also equitable or right.

clue.text: Successfully concluded business in a taciturn manner

explanation.surface: A deal closed by someone who said very little.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal finalised is sewn up; a reserved, uncommunicative person is closed off.

clue.text: Quote makes sound sense

indicators.note: sound means the word is heard, not read

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A quotation that seems reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound sense' reads as good judgement; 'sound' is the homophone signal and 'makes' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote a passage is to cite it as evidence.

clue.text: Voters choose to speak

parts.note: to elect is to choose
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: The voting public pick a candidate to speak for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole body of people entitled to vote in an election.
